name: Pomodoro Sprint
description: Work in a protected 25-minute block, then take a brief intentional break.
steps: Choose one small outcome.
Set a timer for 25 minutes and work on only that outcome.
Stop when the timer rings, mark progress, and take a five-minute break.

name: Active Recall
description: Close the source and pull information from memory before checking what you missed.
steps: Choose a small topic and hide your notes.
Write or say everything you can remember.
Check the source, correct gaps, and test yourself again later.

name: Feynman Explanation
description: Explain an idea in plain language to reveal where your understanding is incomplete.
steps: Write the concept as a heading.
Explain it as if teaching a beginner.
Find vague areas, review them, and simplify the explanation.

name: Blurting
description: Quickly write everything you remember about a topic, then fill the gaps in another color.
steps: Read the topic title and put materials away.
Write every relevant fact you remember.
Compare with your notes and add missing details in another color.

name: Cornell Notes
description: Divide a page into notes, cues, and summary areas so review is built into note-taking.
steps: Divide the page into a wide notes column, a narrow cues column, and a bottom summary.
Capture main ideas in the notes column.
Add questions or keywords in the cues column and summarize after class.

name: Two-Minute Start
description: Shrink the first action until it feels almost too easy, then let momentum decide what comes next.
steps: Name the smallest visible action.
Promise to do only two minutes.
At two minutes, choose freely whether to stop or continue.

name: Spaced Review
description: Revisit material across increasing intervals instead of repeating it all in one sitting.
steps: Create a short set of questions or cards.
Review them today, then after one, three, and seven days.
Shorten the interval for missed items and lengthen it for correct ones.

name: Interleaving
description: Mix related problem types so you practice choosing a method, not only repeating it.
steps: Select two or three related problem types.
Alternate between them rather than completing one full set.
After each problem, name why that method fits.

name: Mind Map
description: Arrange a topic visually around branches to make relationships and missing links easier to see.
steps: Place the main topic in the center.
Add branches for major ideas and smaller branches for evidence or examples.
Draw cross-links where two branches influence each other.

name: SQ3R Reading
description: Survey, question, read, recite, and review to turn a passive chapter into an active task.
steps: Survey headings, images, and summaries, then form questions.
Read to answer each question and recite the answer without looking.
Review the questions and main ideas at the end.

name: Body Doubling
description: Work quietly beside another person and use their presence as a gentle focus cue.
steps: Choose a partner and agree on a work block.
Each person states one outcome before starting.
Work quietly, then share what moved forward at the end.

name: Question Storm
description: Generate questions before searching for answers so curiosity gives the session direction.
steps: Set a timer and write only questions about the topic.
Do not answer or judge them while the timer runs.
Group the questions and choose the most useful one to investigate first.

name: Retrieval Grid
description: Fill a blank grid from memory to compare features, steps, examples, or definitions.
steps: Create row labels for topics and column labels for features.
Hide your notes and fill every cell you can.
Check the grid, correct errors, and retry empty cells.

name: Progressive Summary
description: Compress a page into a paragraph, then a sentence, then a short phrase to find its core idea.
steps: Write a short paragraph that captures the page.
Compress the paragraph into one sentence.
Reduce the sentence to a phrase you can use as a recall cue.

name: Exam Wrapper
description: Review an assessment to separate knowledge gaps, strategy mistakes, and avoidable errors.
steps: Sort missed points by cause: knowledge, method, time, or attention.
Find the pattern that cost the most points.
Write one specific change for the next preparation session.

name: Peer Teach-Back
description: Take turns teaching a small idea while the listener asks for examples and clarification.
steps: Divide the material into small concepts.
Teach one concept without reading from notes.
Let your partner ask questions, then switch roles.

name: Environment Reset
description: Prepare the space, tools, and screen before a work block so fewer choices interrupt you.
steps: Clear the desk except for what this task needs.
Silence notifications and close unrelated tabs.
Place water nearby, open the first resource, and start the timer.

name: Error Log
description: Track mistakes by type and correction so recurring weak points become visible and actionable.
steps: Record the problem, your error, and the correct approach.
Tag the cause, such as concept, setup, calculation, or attention.
Review repeated tags and retry one example from each group.
